thread:
morgan: Heads-up — during the new reranker bring-up I see MRR drop ~3.2% vs baseline on longtail-eval-v2 but NDCG is slightly up (+0.4%).

sarah: Hmm that's a weird divergence. Is this a top-1 vs overall ranking issue or something dataset-specific?

morgan: Looks like top-1 is worse, tail positions slightly better. Full eval output attached below.

morgan: ```
cmd: python tools/eval_rerank.py --model candidate-v2-q4 --dataset longtail-eval-v2 --format "query\n||doc" --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42
results: ndcg@10: 0.642 (+0.004), mrr: 0.285 (-0.032)
```

lee: What changed between baseline and candidate-v2? quant, tokenizer, or prompt formatting?

morgan: Two diffs: 1) PTQ -> hybrid 4-bit on attention weights, 2) we changed the candidate concat order: used `'query \n|| doc'` with a newline delimiter rather than `'query||doc'` (previous).

anil: The formatting change rings alarm bells. We've seen query/doc boundary tokens affect pairwise scores before. Did you verify tokenizers are identical (vocab/fast vs slow)?

morgan: Tokenizer is same model family, but experiments used hf's fast tokenizer for candidate-v2 while baseline used the slow one (longtime legacy). I ran a quick token count diff: some queries gain 2-4 tokens when using fast tokenizer; examples where doc prefix punctuation ends up as separate token.

sarah: That could change pairwise comparisons: extra tokens in query may push order or attention patterns. Any logs showing example failures?

morgan: Pasted two cases:
```
Case A (baseline top1): Q="best way to crop image?"
Candidates: [c1: short answer], [c2: long howto]
Baseline ranked c1 first. candidate-v2 peaks c2. Token diffs: Q baseline tokens 6, fast tokens 8 (adds punctuation tokens).
```

lee: Also check candidate dedupe & truncation. If the delimiter variation changed how we truncate (doc now shifted by one token), KV cache offsets might differ under quantization and affect scores.

anil: Good point. Quantization can amplify small attention differences. Could be a coupling between token boundary shift and low-bit weight noise. Suggest isolating variables: run candidate-v2 with slow tokenizer and run baseline with fast tokenizer (no quant) to see which axis causes MRR drop.

morgan: I'm spinning up three jobs: (A) v2-q4 + fast (current), (B) v2-q4 + slow tokenizer, (C) baseline (no-ptq) + fast tokenizer. Will post results when done.

ops-bot: Job 2112223344 queued: eval-A (v2-q4 + fast)
ops-bot: Job 2112223388 queued: eval-B (v2-q4 + slow)
ops-bot: Job 2112223420 queued: eval-C (baseline + fast)

sarah: Also check dataset provenance. longtail-eval-v2 has some HTML-heavy docs; tokenization shifts with punctuation-heavy inputs can disproportionately affect those examples. Maybe run a slice: html vs plain text.

morgan: Good call — I'll add doc-type slices. Also going to run ndcg@1 to isolate top1 signal.

morgan: Quick interim results (sanity):
- eval-A (v2-q4 + fast): mrr 0.284, ndcg@10 0.643, ndcg@1 0.512
- eval-B (v2-q4 + slow): mrr 0.299, ndcg@10 0.641, ndcg@1 0.536
- eval-C (baseline + fast): mrr 0.297, ndcg@10 0.639, ndcg@1 0.534

anil: So seems quant + fast tokenizer is the worst. Switching tokenizer back improves MRR even with quant. That implies token boundary interaction with quant noise.

lee: Actionable path: 1) standardize tokenizer for onboarding (pick fast or slow) and convert golden sets accordingly, 2) add a token-boundary regression test in the eval harness (compare ndcg@1 with tokenized-length mismatches), 3) run a small calibration sweep on attention quant scales.

sarah: Also add a slice to eval harness for 'short-query_highpunct' — that was where most top1 flips occurred.

morgan: I'll update the onboarding checklist: require tokenizer parity check + run a 'token-boundary' smoke test before flagging model as ready. I'll also create a follow-up ticket to try per-layer quant scaling for attention to see if it reduces top1 flips.

morgan: TL;DR: MRR drop is reproducible when quantization + fast tokenizer + newline delimiter are combined. Next steps: revert delimiter for canary release, standardize tokenizer, and run calibration sweep.

lee: Thanks Morgan. If you want I can help with the calibration job.

morgan: Appreciate it — tagging you for follow-up: @lee. :thumbsup:
